newsitem.title: CHINA: HK Tung wins more popular support on policy goals.
newsitem.headline: HK Tung wins more popular support on policy goals.

text.p: Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa's policy outline for this new region of China has boosted his popular support to its highest level for three months, an opinion poll reported on Monday.
The survey, conducted regularly by the mass-selling Chinese language Ming Pao newspaper since January, climbed within days of Hong Kong's handover to China a week ago.
An inaugural policy speech by Hong Kong's post-colonial leader, setting out goals for housing, education and social welfare, boosted public confidence and trust in his ability, the poll showed.
In the latest survey, which interviewed 2,202 people, the former shipping magnate got an average 5.5 marks out of a total possible score of nine for his competence, and 5.6 for trust.
Elderly citizens tended to give him higher marks.
In an earlier survey in the series, after he unveiled a plan in April to curb civil liberties, Tung scored as low as 4.4 marks for trust and 4.7 for competence.
China took the former British colony back from London on July 1, after 156 years of colonial rule.
